en: The Sūtra on the Great Causes and Conditions for the Benefits of Reciting the Name of the Buddha Amitāyus, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Kang Sengkai of India during the Cao Wei dynasty.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
Together with a multitude of twelve hundred and fifty people whose outflows were exhausted and who had attained mastery of the supernormal powers—
among those noble ones were Venerable Ānanda, Venerable Maudgalyāyana, Venerable Śāriputra, Venerable Mahārṣabha, Venerable Mahākāśyapa, Venerable Gayākāśyapa, and Venerable Mahācunda.
The Venerable Yaśas Kāśyapa, the Venerable Mahāviśuddhacittāśaya, and others such as these served as the leaders;
furthermore, there were the Bodhisattvas Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī, Śraddhāviśuddhi, Prajñā, and Suvimukta,
along with other great *satpuruṣas*, who had fulfilled immeasurable vows and practices and dwelt in inconceivable merit.
An incalculable multitude of bodhisattvas, such as those of virtue, dharma, wisdom, and noble clarity, immediately assembled there.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying: "In the distant past, immeasurable, infinite, and countless kalpas ago..."

There was a great bhikṣu named Dharmākara who encountered countless hundreds of thousands of buddhas and fulfilled immeasurable great vows, surpassing the dharmas practiced by all other buddhas. That bhikṣu Dharmākara has now attained perfect enlightenment;
he currently dwells in the western pure land of Sukhāvatī, known as the Land of Immeasurable Light. He is called Amitāyus.
By the power of that Buddha's original vow, he pervades the worlds of the ten directions with inconceivable majestic spiritual power and proclaims his name,
merits, and virtues with a great voice. Therefore, when all sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions hear and believe in the merits of his name,
they immediately enter the stage of right determination and are born into a pure and blissful buddha-field.
Therefore, among sentient beings, even those who, despite being born as humans, are deaf, blind, mute, foolish, or insane due to their past karma,
shall all attain liberation through the causes and conditions of that Buddha’s light and name. Or,
those who are undergoing incessant suffering within the three miserable realms shall all [attain liberation] through the causes and conditions of that Buddha’s light and name.
If one hears the name of that Buddha’s light and either receives it with faith or recites it,
at that very moment the sins of birth and death from immeasurable and incalculable kalpas will be eliminated. Therefore, Ānanda, if one recites the name of that Buddha—
whether once, ten times, or even up to a hundred thousand times— in every thought-moment, one shall always be protected by the countless transformation Buddhas of Immeasurable Life.
Furthermore, that person shall have two bodhisattvas—one named Avalokiteśvara and one named Mahāsthāmaprāpta—as their leaders;
these two bodhisattvas, together with a multitude of great bodhisattvas, will constantly come to protect them.
After their life comes to an end, they will be reborn in that Land of Utmost Bliss and Purity of Amitāyus. Therefore, Ānanda, even if a fierce fire were to fill [the world],...
In the three thousand great thousandfold world-systems, there will surely be those who, having heard and believed in the name of that Buddha, are called "White Lotus Flowers Born from Fire.
This is known as the inconceivable cause and condition for the great matter of the benefit of the name.
By the power of that Buddha’s original vow, all Buddhas of the ten directions together praise the merit and virtue of that Buddha’s name.
Furthermore, because he praises those sentient beings who practice mindfulness of the Buddha, you all should faithfully accept the name of that Buddha.
The World-Honored One said to Ānanda: "The reason the Tathāgata has appeared in the world is to speak of that Buddha, which [others] cannot [fully comprehend]."
Because this matter of the causes and conditions for the great benefit of the light of the true merits of inconceivable names is difficult to encounter,
difficult to see, difficult to obtain, and difficult to hear, I say that if there are sentient beings who hear this Dharma, they should all believe and comply with it,
practicing in accordance with the Dharma.

The World-Honored One told Ānanda: "That Bhikṣu Dharmākara, in order to deliver all sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions, gave rise to world-transcending vows and cultivated immeasurable great practices. This was his original, long-ago, true accomplishment;
he is the eternally abiding Dharma-body, the Buddha of Immeasurable Life. By means of his inconceivable power of majestic spiritual authority, he pervades the ten directions."

In order to teach and establish countless sentient beings in this world upon the unsurpassed path of truth, he may manifest as a Kṣatriya king or a universal monarch (cakravartin), or as a householder, a noble, or one of great wealth and status;

or as a king of the six heavens of the desire realm or a Brahmā king; or even as the body of a being in hell, a hungry ghost, an animal, or an asura—constantly employing the four [means of attraction].
Is the one who manifested through majestic deportment as all Ānandas, who has long since truly accomplished the eternally abiding Dharma-body as the Buddha of Immeasurable Life,
anyone other than me? It is I, the World-Honored One, who today,
out of compassion for you all sentient beings who dwell in the great darkness of the night of ignorance, have appeared here in this degenerate age from that realm of non-action in Sukhāvatī.
In this world of evil, such as the royal capital of Kāya, the names of those Buddhas and the causes and conditions for their inconceivable merits are said to be difficult to encounter,
difficult to see, difficult to attain, and difficult to hear. Therefore,
any sentient beings who hear this sutra should all believe and accept it, practicing according to the Dharma.

The World-Honored One told Ānanda: "Even if all sentient beings were to have afflictions, evil karma, deep obstructions, and heavy retributions, the light, name, and spiritual power of that Buddha would remain unobstructed and attainable.
For this reason, that Buddha is named 'Unobstructed and Unopposed Pure Wisdom' and 'Joyful Equal Wisdom. Because his wisdom is unobstructed, his majestic spiritual power is likewise unobstructed."
Because power is non-apprehensible, great compassion is also non-apprehensible.

Therefore, in this turbid and evil world, if all sentient beings—with their limited wisdom characterized by apprehension—entertain doubts regarding the Buddha’s non-apprehending wisdom, inconceivable wisdom, immeasurable wisdom, the supreme wisdom of the Mahāyāna, and the peerless, most excellent wisdom, they will remain in doubt and lack faith; and because of these doubts, [they suffer].
Throughout countless *kalpas*, one may fall into the Caṇḍāla hell or enter the Piṇḍāra hell, undergoing endless suffering with no prospect of escape.

Therefore, if any sentient being possesses right faith and wisdom in the Buddha, they shall immediately enter the stage of certainty (*samyaktva-niyāma*) and become non-retrogressive regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. This is called the inconceivable merit.
The Buddha has spoken this sutra regarding the great causal conditions for the benefit of the name and title of his virtue;
at that moment, the entire great earth shook in six ways, and the heavens rained down exquisite flowers.

Spontaneously, from the midst of the sky, there arose a subtle and wondrous great voice praising the inconceivable light and the pure name of the Buddha Amitāyus, as well as the great matter of benefit spoken today by the World-Honored One.
Furthermore, when the World-Honored One preached this sutra, immeasurable sentient beings resolved their minds upon the unsurpassed, right, and true path;
gods and humans attained the fruit of Anāgāmin; and the great Bodhisattvas adorned their merit with the four great vows, destined to achieve perfect enlightenment in a future age.
After the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the assembly of great Bodhisattvas...
The great śrāvaka disciples, including Ānanda and others, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced, prostrated before the Buddha, and departed.
This is the *Sūtra on the Great Causes and Conditions for the Benefits of Reciting the Name of the Buddha Amitāyus*.
